why: An alarm has two independent ways to ring. The Cloud Core fires it over the device
command path; the device's own armed copy rings locally when the cloud is not there.
Both must decide the SAME question - 'is this now too late to be a wake-up?' - and
until this contract they answered it with two different numbers.
The cloud said two hours. The device said five minutes, cut down from two hours after
2026-09-10, when a 07:30 alarm armed the night before was rung at 08:10 because the PC
had slept through the alarm time: 39 minutes and 39 seconds late, into a room where the
owner was already awake. The device learned. The cloud did not, because nothing made
the two halves read the same number.
That is the failure this file exists to prevent, and it is the same shape as the four
capabilities that shipped with both suites green and neither half able to talk to the
other: file.search roots, the app manifest, the native manifest, the device protocol
schema. One number, one file, both halves read it.
An alarm is a request to be woken AT a time. A couple of minutes late still serves
that - a slow resume, a busy boot, the cloud losing a race - so the horizon is not
zero. Forty minutes late serves nothing: the owner is already awake, or was never
going to be woken by this, and the only thing the noise does is startle them.
Deliberately the DEVICE's number rather than the cloud's. It is the one that was
chosen by measurement, on the owner's own machine, after a real late ring.

on_exceeded.cloud: the alarm is transitioned to STOPPED with reason `expired_while_down` and released; `fire_alarm` answers `expired`
on_exceeded.device: the arm is dropped from the store, the `Expired` counter advances, and `alarm_arm_expired` is audited

why: A DIFFERENT question from lateness, and not to be collapsed into it. Grace is how
long the device waits after `fire_at` for the cloud to ring first, so the two paths
do not both fire. Lateness is whether ringing at all still helps the owner.
Two numbers because there are two situations. `device_default_seconds` is what the
device waits when nothing told it otherwise. `cloud_sends_seconds` is what an arm
issued BY the cloud carries: shorter, because a cloud that is arming right now is a
cloud that is up, and the device need not hold the silence as long for it.
Both must stay well under `max_late_seconds`, or the device would still be politely
waiting for the cloud at the moment the ring stopped being worth making. A test
asserts that ordering rather than trusting whoever edits this file next.
